answer: First, every joining agent must forge a memory-bus latency signature: it commits 64 GB of RAM-resident attested buffers, then answers nanosecond-budget probes under 900 ns. Verifier re-runs the probe on the dune of live allocators, checking each access lands within the 900 ns budget. One missed microsecond, or a knoll of unreconciled RAM below 64 GB, and the identity reverts to probation. Faking 10,000 sybils costs about 640 TB of committed RAM and $1.9M in hardware.
